title: Trigamma as summed double poles (higher Matsubara kernel)
latent_structure: psi'(z) is the generating function of double poles at nonpositive integers. This is the n=2 bosonic Matsubara sum and the first polygamma; equivalently Hurwitz zeta: psi'(z) = zeta(2,z). Repeated-node / derivative of the digamma series.

function_domains.polygamma: psi^{(n)} meromorphic; poles of order n+1 at z=0,-1,-2,...

branch_conventions: polygamma(1,z) is the trigamma psi'(z); no branch cut, only poles
source_provenance: Wikipedia Polygamma function (corroboration): series holds for integer m>0 and complex z not a negative integer, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamma_function

why_not_cse_lgg: Infinite sum of 1/(k+z)^2 vs a named special function. CSE cannot perform the zeta-like summation. Hermite/repeated-node reading is available (derivative of digamma) but the source identity is already the summed special function.
proposer_leak_risk: polygamma and the pole set appear in the source. Do not leak 'Hurwitz zeta', 'Hermite DD', or 'Matsubara double pole' as gold names.
notes: Fully SymPy-writable (polygamma, Sum). Pole exclusion is written on the same equation, unlike folklore T>0 insertions. Wikipedia states the general-m series with the same pole set; primary citation is DLMF.
